title: LIVORA
description:
LIVORA is a choice-driven life simulation about trying to build a good life when money, work, relationships, health, family, assets, time and the wider world keep pulling you in different directions.

Choose where your story begins, decide what matters most and shape a life that feels genuinely yours.

One day, you might be deciding whether to work overtime, help someone you care about or protect the little energy you have left. The next, you could be planning a date, preparing for a job interview, exploring a new investment or trying to afford a holiday without creating a financial disaster.

Every part of your life is connected. Earning more may improve your finances while damaging your wellbeing. Supporting someone else may leave your own responsibilities unfinished. Buying an asset could create new opportunities while adding costs and pressure. Playing it safe can protect what you have, while taking a risk could change everything.

There is rarely a perfect choice.

Only the life your decisions create.

BUILD YOUR LIFE, ONE DAY AT A TIMEBegin from a range of starting lives, each with different circumstances, responsibilities, pressures and opportunities.

Your starting point affects the challenges ahead, but it does not decide who you will become.

Make daily decisions about money, work, relationships, health, family, personal time and long-term ambitions. Deal with urgent problems, follow unexpected opportunities and decide what can wait when life asks for more than you can give.

Some days will feel manageable.

Others will force you to choose what matters most.

PLAN DAYS THAT FEEL LIKE YOURSUse the Day Planner Map to decide how your free time unfolds.

Choose where to go, what to do and who to spend time with. Plan activities across the morning, afternoon and evening while considering their cost, travel time, energy demands and effect on the people around you.

Sleep in, recover at home, visit family, meet friends, work on a hobby, go shopping, take care of unfinished responsibilities or build an entire day around doing something memorable.

Your plans can change what becomes available later. Spending too much in the afternoon may limit your evening. Resting may restore your energy but leave something important unresolved. A successful activity could lead to an unexpected invitation or create a moment that changes the rest of the day.

Some days may become Days Worth Remembering: permanent Life memories shaped by the people, places, choices and trade-offs that made them matter.

BUILD RELATIONSHIPS THAT EVOLVEThe people in your life have their own personalities, needs, expectations and memories.

The Relationship Hub brings the complete story of a romantic relationship together in one place.

Follow:

• Your partner’s personality and current relationship stage

• Connection, stability and pressure

• Recent relationship moments

• Upcoming plans

• Active issues

• Important milestones

• The complete journey you have shared

• Actions available at the current stage

The information available changes as the relationship develops. A new romance will feel different from a serious partnership, a marriage, a growing family or a relationship that has ended.

Plan and play through dates by choosing what to do, where to go, when to meet and how much to spend. Your available options may be affected by your schedule, finances, energy, weather, location and the current state of the relationship.

When the date arrives, make choices that can strengthen your connection, create tension or lead to important conversations.

CONVERSATIONS, ISSUES AND REPAIRPartners can raise concerns, ask difficult questions and respond to what has been happening in both of your lives.

Relationship issues may develop from:

• Unanswered messages

• Money disagreements

• A lack of quality time

• Work pressure

• Unequal responsibilities

• Different plans for the future

• Family interference

• Broken trust

How you respond matters. Some problems can be repaired quickly, while others may continue affecting the relationship over time.

SHAPE A SHARED LIFERelationships can progress through exclusivity, commitment, living together, engagement, marriage and family life.

Discuss whether you are ready to become serious, move in together or take the next major step. Progress is influenced by the complete relationship history rather than guaranteed by selecting a button.

Moving in together can affect:

• Housing

• Rent and bills

• Commutes

• Household responsibilities

• Personal space

• Daily routines

• Relationship pressure

Living together can bring people closer, but it can also reveal problems that were easier to ignore before.

PROPOSALS, ENGAGEMENTS AND WEDDINGSPlan a proposal by choosing its timing, location, style and budget.

Your partner’s response can depend on trust, commitment, recent tension and previous conversations about the future.

An accepted proposal can lead to wedding planning, where decisions about the ceremony, venue, guests, budget, date, family involvement and honeymoon turn the wedding into a major playable life event.

MARRIAGE AND FAMILY LIFEMarriage is not the end of the relationship journey.

Married and cohabiting couples must continue balancing:

• Shared finances

• Household responsibilities

• Careers

• Personal space

• Time together

• Long-term plans

• Family expectations

• Relationship pressure

Small imbalances can become meaningful problems when they are repeatedly ignored.

Couples may also discuss whether they want children, whether they feel ready and what needs to change first.

Housing, finances, careers, childcare, support networks and relationship stability can all influence the decision.

Becoming parents introduces new relationships, responsibilities, pressures and moments that can shape the whole family.

FACE SEPARATION AND CHANGENot every relationship will last forever.

Couples may ask for space, separate, end an unmarried relationship or begin divorce proceedings.

These changes can affect:

• Housing

• Finances

• Shared possessions

• Children

• Family relationships

• Future plans

• Emotional wellbeing

Where children are involved, former partners may need to manage parenting schedules, maintenance, communication and important decisions together.

The history of the relationship remains visible even after it ends, preserving the moments, decisions and consequences that shaped it.

Every relationship can develop differently.

What you say matters.

What you avoid saying can matter just as much.

STAY CONNECTED THROUGH GROUP CHATSPlayable Group Chats let you take part in active conversations, respond to plans, react to messages, vote in polls and influence what happens next.

You may need to commit, set boundaries, suggest an alternative, support someone or deal with the consequences of staying silent.

Friends and family remember whether you showed up, kept your promises and made space for them when it mattered.

PREPARE FOR LIFE’S BIG EVENTSWeddings, birthdays, nights out and other major social occasions develop over time.

Receive invitations, respond before the deadline, manage the expected cost and prepare for what the event may require. Decide whether to attend, bring someone, set a budget, ask for help, leave early or suggest a different plan.

Then experience the event itself and live with what follows.

A brilliant evening could strengthen a relationship, create a lasting memory or lead somewhere unexpected. An expensive decision, awkward conversation or broken commitment may still be affecting your life long after everyone has gone home.

BUILD A CAREER, NOT JUST A SALARYExplore career opportunities based on your circumstances, qualifications, experience and current suitability.

Compare salary, working arrangements, pressure, flexibility and the effect a role could have on the rest of your life. Apply immediately, save an opportunity for later or decide that the trade-off is not worth it.

Applications can lead to interview invitations. Prepare by researching the employer, reviewing the role, practising questions and reflecting on your experience.

During interviews, choose how to answer role-specific questions. Your preparation, evidence, circumstances and responses all contribute to the result.

You may receive feedback, face rejection, earn an offer or discover the areas holding you back.

A better salary can create new possibilities, but work can also demand more time, energy and emotional capacity than expected.

Success is not only about how far you climb.

It is about what happens to the life behind your career.

PLAN TIME AWAYRequest annual leave and plan holidays around your available time, responsibilities and budget.

Consider where to go, how long to stay, what the trip will cost and who will come with you. Decide whether to keep things affordable, spend more for a better experience or postpone the trip until life feels more stable.

A holiday can offer recovery, connection and memories that last.

It can also create financial pressure, workplace complications and difficult choices before you have even left.

MANAGE A CONNECTED LIFEYour decisions can affect:

• Money, rent, bills, savings, debt and investments

• Work, applications, interviews and career progression

• Energy, physical health and mental load

• Romantic relationships, friendships and family

• Stability, confidence, wellbeing and self-respect

• Time, annual leave, holidays and social commitments

• Housing, businesses, properties, vehicles and possessions

• Unfinished responsibilities and future consequences

These systems do not exist separately.

Financial pressure can damage your health. Career decisions can strengthen or strain your relationships. A difficult period at work can follow you home. Time spent helping someone else may leave your own problems unresolved.

Protecting one part of life may require sacrificing another.

MANAGE MONEY UNDER PRESSUREHandle rent, bills, debt, subscriptions, unexpected costs and everyday spending while trying to protect your future.

Decide what must be paid now, what can wait and whether taking on more work is worth the personal cost.

A healthy income does not guarantee a stable life. Higher earnings may bring greater responsibility, less free time and more pressure. A cheap decision may solve today’s problem while creating a larger one later.

Money affects what you can do, where you can go, who you can help and how easily you can recover when life changes unexpectedly.

BUILD AND MANAGE YOUR ASSETSUse the Asset Vault to manage everything you own and explore opportunities for your future.

Your Portfolio brings your businesses, properties and vehicles together in one place.

Review:

• The total value of your holdings

• Your available cash

• Your businesses, properties and vehicles

• Your most valuable asset

• Your latest acquisition

Explore the Market to discover new opportunities. Filter and compare available assets, see what you already own and understand exactly how much more money you need when something remains out of reach.

Each asset can provide clear information about:

• Purchase price

• Current value

• Potential benefits

• Ongoing costs

• Ownership status

• Requirements that must be met

Before completing a purchase, review its cost and the money you will have remaining. Once acquired, the asset immediately becomes part of your Portfolio.

Some opportunities may provide income or stability. Others may improve convenience, unlock possibilities or support the kind of Life you are trying to build.

Every purchase involves a trade-off.

What strengthens your future may place pressure on your present.

LIVE IN A WORLD THAT KEEPS MOVINGYour life does not exist in isolation.

Seasons change. Weather can disrupt plans and influence daily decisions. World News brings fictional events, sporting results, economic developments and wider changes that continue beyond your immediate life.

New technology, rising costs, changing opportunities and major events can affect work, travel, finances and the future you are trying to build.

The world keeps moving whether you are ready or not.

Your life has to move with it.

YOUR LIFE REMEMBERSChoices in LIVORA do not disappear once the moment has passed.

Ignored messages, missed payments, delayed decisions, broken promises, relationship conflicts, career sacrifices, health concerns and unfinished responsibilities can return days, months or years later.

People remember how you treated them. Financial problems grow when ignored. Work pressure affects life outside your job. Decisions made during difficult moments can follow you into completely different stages of your life.

Relationship journeys preserve the milestones, conflicts, commitments and changes you experienced together.

Weekly summaries and long-term reports reveal the patterns behind your choices: what protected you, what repeatedly cost you and what kind of life you are gradually creating.

A small decision may become an opportunity, a lasting consequence or a problem you still need to face.

START AGAIN AND CHOOSE DIFFERENTLYEvery new life is an opportunity to approach things differently.

Choose another starting point. Handle money with more care. Protect your energy. Prioritise your relationships. Pursue a different career. Take greater risks. Build a portfolio. Start a family. Create a shared life. Make the choices you avoided before.

A single different decision can change what happens next.

A different pattern of choices can create an entirely different life.

There is no single correct way to play LIVORA.

The question is not whether you made every perfect decision.

The question is what kind of life your decisions created.

FEATURES• Choice-driven life simulation set under modern pressure

• Multiple starting lives with different difficulties and circumstances

• Decisions with immediate, delayed and long-term consequences

• A map-based Day Planner with playable free-time activities

• Full-day experiences with morning, afternoon and evening plans

• Playable weekends, nights out and special occasions

• A complete Relationship Hub covering dating, commitment, shared life, marriage, family changes and separation

• Playable dates shaped by time, money, energy, weather, location and relationship history

• Relationship conversations, issues, milestones and lasting shared memories

• Moving in, proposals, wedding planning, marriage and family life

• Separation, divorce and co-parenting consequences

• Group Chats with messages, reactions, polls and meaningful replies

• Major social events with invitations, countdowns, preparation and aftermath

• Career opportunities, applications, interview preparation, interviews and offers

• Annual leave, holiday planning and playable trips

• Money, rent, bills, debt, savings, assets and financial pressure

• An Asset Vault for managing your complete Portfolio

• A Market containing businesses, properties and vehicles

• Asset prices, values, benefits, requirements and ongoing costs

• Relationships, friendships, family, health and personal wellbeing

• Changing weather, World News and future developments

• Days Worth Remembering and permanent Life memories

• Weekly summaries and long-term reports

• Multiple paths, outcomes and highly replayable lives

• Thoughtful, text-led gameplay designed to be played at your own pace

BUILD A LIFE. SURVIVE THE COST.
description_short: LIVORA is a choice-driven life simulation where money, work, relationships, health, family, assets and time all connect. Plan your days, build a career, deepen relationships, manage your portfolio and live with consequences that can shape your life for years.
